limits: No push, live approvals, real missions, model provider tests, live restarts, other profiles, destructive changes

items.title: Make authorization delivery recoverable
items.why: A valid approval must not disappear between being consumed and being queued. A recovery path must also avoid accidental duplicate execution.
items.action: Define durable states for authorized, queued, started, and terminal commands. Choose a minimal outbox or recovery protocol using stable command IDs, replay rules, and idempotency. Keep the existing command path; do not introduce a second scheduler.
acceptance: Inject a failure after each durable write and recover after a process restart.
Each command is either delivered once at dispatch level, explicitly rejected, or marked unresolved for operator review; no silent disappearance.
Repeated HTTP/WS responses, worker retries, and restarts cannot enqueue a second runnable copy.
Document that deduplicated dispatch does not guarantee exactly-once external side effects.
items.dependency: Agree on the recovery contract before changing write order. R05 adds the diagnostic surface.
items.permission: Local implementation needs a separate work order. Never test by approving real pending commands.

items.title: Do not call a minimal contract a validated success
items.why: A green pass can imply more evidence than the validator actually has.
items.action: Define explicit semantics for evidence missing, structural checks passed, needs human review, and verified success. Default insufficient contracts to needs-human-review or a separate non-success state. Keep command completion distinct from task acceptance.
acceptance: Regression: auto-generated contract, empty goal, and a failing non-critical check never produce validated success.
Missing reviewer, missing artifacts, or empty behavioral evidence cannot silently upgrade a task to verified success.
The UI exposes the checks and limitations behind the verdict.
Existing valid contracts retain their documented pass/fail behavior.
items.dependency: Audit callers and persisted verdict compatibility before changing the enum. Independent review automation is R14, not a prerequisite.
items.permission: No autonomous merge or acceptance-policy change without Cristóbal's approval.

items.title: Enforce step timeout and truthful cancellation
items.why: The step deadline can expire while the caller still waits for the worker thread. A cancellation label also does not prove process exit.
items.action: Define cancellation ownership across runner, process group, and step executor. Do not replace the context with shutdown(wait=False) and call that termination. Propagate a cancellation signal and confirm owned-process exit, or show stop unconfirmed. Prevent retries while prior work is still running.
acceptance: A controlled hanging runner returns within the documented deadline and cleanup budget, without waiting for normal completion.
Owned child and grandchild processes are terminated or explicitly reported as unconfirmed; unrelated processes are untouched.
Retries never overlap an unresolved earlier attempt.
A recycled PID cannot receive a stop request meant for an older process identity; the UI separates requested cancellation from confirmed exit.
items.dependency: R01 lifecycle and E08 identity. Keep observation and termination as separate contracts.
items.permission: Use inert fixtures and scratch processes only. Do not cancel live agents or restart the live bridge as a test.

items.title: Publish a per-route execution protection matrix
items.why: A pre-launch scanner is not a sandbox, and a Docker policy does not protect a direct host CLI path.
items.action: List each supported HTTP/CLI/container execution route, its approval boundary, launch checks, mounts, network policy, secret handling, audit, and known bypass surface. Test the matrix instead of adding a broad host-monitoring subsystem.
acceptance: Every supported adapter is mapped to its actual launch and audit calls.
An unsafe supported container configuration is rejected in a route-level test.
Direct-host execution is labeled as trusted-operator execution, not sandboxed execution.
Documentation makes no claim of continuous runtime supervision unless such supervision is implemented and exercised.
items.dependency: Decide which adapters are officially supported before expanding them.
items.permission: No eBPF, Landlock rollout, wider privileges, or changed host policy without an explicit architecture decision.

items.title: Show loaded code and audit capability without exposing secrets
items.why: The source tree can be newer than a running process, while a green health check says little about loaded features or durable audit signatures.
items.action: Add a privacy-safe diagnostic snapshot to an existing surface: loaded commit/build, start time, relevant capabilities, read/write-store status, and persistent/ephemeral audit-key mode. Return booleans or capability states, never secret material.
acceptance: Changing the checkout without restart does not change the reported loaded build.
Missing endpoint is shown as unknown/unsupported, never as feature absent or healthy by default.
Ephemeral audit mode is visibly distinguished from persistent cross-restart verification.
Diagnostics never include tokens, keys, environment dumps, prompts, or argv.
items.dependency: Choose build attestation that survives editable local development. Coordinate safe activation with active agents.
items.permission: Checking live configuration must not reveal secret values. Restart only with an agreed safe window.

items.title: Replace the historical feature inventory with a current one
items.why: Stale documentation can send the next agent to reimplement a feature, revive a retired subsystem, or promise a guarantee that does not exist.
items.action: Reconcile SCOPE, ROADMAP, README, security notes, and RepoCiv skills against current code. Mark active, experimental, retired, and reference-only components. Keep this HTML as a dated review, not a second canonical backlog.
acceptance: No item is both implemented and retired without a dated explanation.
2D and 3D remain official; expiry and position hooks are not listed as missing.
Each active subsystem has one source-of-truth document and an evidence pointer.
Correct the AgentCraft comparison's authentication claim, review-failure semantics, and unreproducible score.
items.dependency: Cristóbal confirms disputed product boundaries. Current code is evidence, not automatic permission to keep a subsystem.
items.permission: Do not delete code or revive retired features as part of a documentation cleanup.

items.title: Reconcile interrupted tasks before any restart replay
items.why: A disk checkpoint does not, by itself, restore a live registry or prove that prior work stopped.
items.action: Define interrupted task states and rebuild a read-only recovery view at startup. Identify owned surviving work before offering an explicit resume. Never automatically replay an external side effect. Include authoritative-store backup and isolated restore tests.
acceptance: Restart a scratch bridge with persisted executing/blocked tasks and show them as interrupted or blocked, not silently absent or completed.
A surviving process is correlated by stable identity before a resume or stop decision.
Restoring a checkpoint never renews approval deadlines or silently repeats completed external actions.
The restore procedure identifies authoritative stores, derived caches, permissions, version compatibility, and unresolved records.
items.dependency: R01 recovery invariants, R03 process ownership, and R05 diagnostic identity.
items.permission: Use scratch state only. A checkpoint is not permission to resume an agent, overwrite live state, or restart the service.

items.title: Confine repository and issue IDs before filesystem access
items.why: A malformed identifier can resolve outside the intended state-store root, even in a single-operator alpha. Approval does not make a malformed path safe.
items.action: Define literal identifier formats and reject malformed values before any side effect. Use component-aware resolved-path confinement at each store boundary, including symlink handling. Decide whether task_run is an officially supported command before documenting its risk and policy.
acceptance: Parent-directory IDs, absolute paths, separators, malformed values, and symlink escapes are rejected before mkdir/read/write/delete.
Valid repository identifiers retain collision-free storage mapping; do not silently normalize invalid tokens.
HTTP/WS/direct helper tests share the identifier contract and contain writes within scratch roots.
A trusted token or approval cannot bypass the store-boundary check.
items.dependency: R06 supported-surface decision. Fix store helpers even if a command is later retired.
items.permission: Test only path construction and scratch stores. Do not probe user files or label this a remote exploit without proving reachability and authorization conditions.
